messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — gpu-queue-length for pool 'model-llama-2-usw' spiked to 98% of capacity; sustained queue growth for 6m. Autoscaler attempting launches but failing. See logs: quota errors. Paging oncall.
Alex: oncall-ml here, looking. Thanks for the page.
Kat: I'm watching runtime logs now. Autoscaler logs show repeated errors: `ComputeApiError: quotaExceeded: REGION_GPU_QUOTA` and `InstanceCreateFailed: insufficient quota for nvidia-tesla`. Also seeing 429s from frontend -> router: "no available backend".
Maria: I'm joining — what customer impact do we have?
Alex: We've got elevated 429s for a subset of requests routed to us-west1. Per token metrics: 95th latency up 3x for queued requests. CS reported a handful of customers seeing request failures: Liz, can you confirm?
Liz (cust-succ): Yes, two customers (enterprise orgs) reported errors and timeouts starting ~11:02 UTC. They're seeing "service unavailable" and we have tickets open.
Kat: Confirmed queue length metrics: queue depth jumped from ~120 -> 1800 across user-priority buckets in 6 minutes. Autoscaler kept retrying but cloud returned quota errors. There's no immediate OOM or kernel crash.
Alex: Do we have spare capacity in secondary regions? Can we route overflow to eu-west1 temporarily?
Jay: infra here — eu-west1 has capacity but also limited GPU quota. We have ~40% free there for this model; should be usable for spill traffic but need routing change and possibly a model-variant downgrade to a quantized variant to fit some requests.
Kat: Two mitigation options: 1) emergency cross-region spill to eu-west1 (routing change) + downgrade non-SLAs to quantized variant; 2) throttle low-priority customers and preserve capacity for paid/enterprise.
Alex: Let's do both: immediate routing to eu-west1 for new requests, and throttle best-effort traffic. Keep enterprise unaffected if possible.
Maria: I'll implement a temporary route policy and throttle script. Alex, handoff to me in 15 if you're stepping away.
Kat: Routing CLI I'm using: `redwoodctl routing set --pool model-llama-2 --policy emergency --actions "route:eu-west1@0.6,us-west1@0.4" --match "!enterprise"` — that will route 60% of non-enterprise traffic to eu-west1.
Alex: Deploy-bot, please checkpoint the routing change.
deploy-bot: Routing change requested by Maria. Review required. Approving as emergency change.
Maria: Pushed the policy. Observability: starting to see new connections hitting eu-west1. Queue depth in us-west1 dropped from 1800 -> 900 in 4m.
Kat: Also toggled auto-fallback to quantized-llama-2-small for best-effort requests: `redwoodctl model fallback --pool model-llama-2 --variant quantized-small --filter "priority:low"` — LGTM. Non-enterprise now get quantized variant in eu-west1.
Liz (cust-succ): Incident note: two enterprise customers still see intermittent 429s but less frequent. Ticket owners updated.
Alex: How about autoscaler failures — can we get quota increased or spin reserved capacity?
Jay: I'm opening a support case with cloud provider for immediate GPU quota bump; in parallel we can spin reserved GCP nodes via our Infra emergency pool if we convert some preemptible reservations to on-demand. That will take ~12–18m to register and join the pool.
Kat: Logs show reason for failure: our autoscaler attempted zone provisioning that exceeds vGPU quota. Autoscaler attempted 6 times with 5m backoff.
Maria: Temporarily increased request-level throttles to protect control plane: `trafficctl rate-limit --pool model-llama-2 --global 1500rps` — implemented.
Alex: Noted. Any risk of violating latency SLOs for enterprise after these changes?
Kat: Enterprise is pinned to us-west1 and we prioritized it in routing. They should be fine except brief retries while in-flight requests drain.
Liz (cust-succ): Customers acknowledged our update and appreciate the priority handling.
Alex: Maria, can you take lead on on-call until this stabilizes? I'll head for a quick break; ping me if escalation needed.
Maria: Taking over oncall. I'll keep monitoring.
Maria: Update 11:28 UTC — queue depth leveling: us-west1 ~400, eu-west1 handling ~700. 95th latency trending down.
Jay: Cloud support replied — quota increase subject to approval; they can provision additional GPUs within 30–45 minutes. I'm requesting emergency capacity now.
Kat: We're still seeing a small number of 429s for long-running batched requests. I've reduced batch size for non-enterprise to shrink per-request resource need: `model-config update --pool model-llama-2 --batch-size 4 --filter "priority:low"`.
Maria: Good call. Observability shows decreased memory pressure on hosts.
deploy-bot: Autoscaler attempted manual scale: 6 -> 18 nodes; last 4 failed due to quota. Two succeeded in eu-west1.
Maria: Good — eu-west1 nodes came up and the pool is more balanced.
Alex: Any customer escalations pending?
Liz (cust-succ): One enterprise asked for an RCA timeline. We're collecting notes.
Kat: Root cause notes so far: sudden traffic spike to us-west1 combined with exhausted GPU quota and autoscaler retries exposed lack of cross-region warm capacity. Also missing an automated fallback to quantized variants earlier.
Maria: Current status 11:40 UTC: traffic stabilized, us-west1 queue ~250, eu-west1 ~420, overall 429 rate back to baseline. Cloud quota approval pending; infra will add capacity when approved.
Alex: Thanks team. I'll be available on slack. Maria, keep watch and escalate to SRE manager if quota not resolved in 45m.
Maria: Will do. Postmortem owners: Kat (runtime), Jay (infra), Alex (oncall timeline), Liz (customer comms). I'll start an incident doc.
Alex: Handing off formally to Maria at 11:43 UTC. Good job everyone.
incident-bot: Incident severity lowered to S2 at 11:50 UTC. Continue monitoring.
